clue.text: Go for Mailsort — it's the best choice

parts.note: to go for something is to opt for it

indicators.note: to sort letters is to put them into a new order, so the word mail is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the first part of the run-together word

explanation.surface: An advert urging customers to choose the Royal Mail's Mailsort service as the best option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mailsort' reads as one postal product, but it splits into a word and 'sort', the anagram signal; 'Go for' is the idiom for choosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optimal is the most favourable possibility, the best one available.

clue.text: Work in pad over in town …

definitions.note: the answer means of a town or a town-dweller, while the clue word is the place itself

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: over in the sense of knocked over or upset, so the letters of in pad are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Going to work in someone's flat in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram with 'pad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppidan means of a town, or a town-dweller, from Latin oppidum, a town.

clue.text: … nevertheless needing time for contemplation

parts.note: though can mean nevertheless, as in 'he came, though'

explanation.surface: A continuation of the previous clue: going to town but still needing time to reflect.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is the act of thinking, reflection or contemplation.

clue.text: Odd time to get in right talent

indicators.note: the letter for right gets into the word time
odd means strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange moment to bring in the right talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' suggests alternate letters, but here it rearranges TIME with R put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, so here a quality or ability, talent.

clue.text: It helps to see how to get over a bad situation

parts.note: lam means a quick escape, a way out of trouble, as in on the lam
a plight is a bad situation

explanation.surface: Advice on how to recover from a difficult predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as self-help; LAM is mainly American slang for escaping.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the light given by a lamp, which lets one see in the dark.

clue.text: Fish taken where it's landed

parts.note: had is the past participle of have, meaning taken
a dock is where a catch or cargo is brought ashore

explanation.surface: A fish described by being caught and brought ashore at the quay.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: A bird gets no promotion from the lady

parts.note: her refers to the lady

indicators.note: in a down clue, promotion lifts the word no upwards, reading it backwards

explanation.surface: A woman refuses to give a bird a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'promotion' raises NO to ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Stomach disorder caused by odd days without a drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled days go around the drink
odd means strange, so the letters of days are rearranged

parts.note: Pepsi is a brand of cola drink

explanation.surface: Indigestion brought on by strange days going without drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled 'odd' days wrap round the drink rather than doing without it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, a disorder of the stomach.

clue.text: Herb, a Shakespearean in spectacles

indicators.note: the character sits inside the spectacles

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean character wearing glasses is named after a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb used in cooking.

clue.text: Lines written to a girl at a terminal

indicators.note: the lines are written after the girl's name

parts.note: Kath is a girl's name
an ode is lines of verse

explanation.surface: A love poem composed for a girl waiting at a station terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathode is an old spelling of cathode, the negative terminal of an electrical device.

clue.text: Plan for bringing back Thatcher — not half!

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: bringing something back turns it round, so the shortened name is read backwards
only half of the name is kept, the second half dropped

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, the former British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A political scheme in support of restoring Thatcher to power, offered with emphatic enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much', but here it keeps half of the Prime Minister's first name; 'bringing back' turns that half round.
explanation.definitionFit: A program, the American spelling of programme, is a scheme or plan of action.

clue.text: Anyhow, sceptre commands it

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, disordered way, so the letters of sceptre are jumbled

explanation.surface: Whatever else happens, the royal sceptre is a symbol that commands deference.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a sceptre, emblem of royal authority, is what commands this.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect is the esteem or deference that authority, symbolised by a monarch's sceptre, is able to command.

clue.text: Drug for fingernail treatment

parts.note: a digit is a finger

indicators.note: treatment works the letters of nail over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking which medicine is used on a damaged fingernail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fingernail' reads as one word but splits in two: 'finger' gives a synonym, and 'nail' is rearranged by 'treatment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalin is a heart medicine extracted from foxglove, a drug.

clue.text: Time to amuse, they say

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone passing the hours by finding something to entertain themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'amuse, they say': said aloud, 'amuse' is 'a Muse', and Erato is one of the nine Muses, of lyric poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: The rump, of course

definitions.meaning: the rump or buttock end of beef, an old butchery term
a slangy clipping of naturally, meaning obviously

explanation.definitionFit: Natch is both an old word for the rump of beef and slang shortening of naturally, meaning of course.

clue.text: Reactionary is sure to take cover first

indicators.note: the cover goes ahead of the word for sure

parts.note: to hide is to cover
bound means certain, sure

explanation.surface: A conservative person is bound to run for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound means narrow-minded and resistant to change, reactionary.

clue.text: Model after the boys has gone out with an old politician

indicators.note: gone is spread out around the other pieces, sitting on the outside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the model letter follows the boys

parts.note: lads are boys
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: A fashion model has walked out with an elderly statesman, leaving the boys behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' tells you that gone sits on the outside, round the boys and the car; 'Model' looks like a fashion model but is Ford's Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was a Victorian Liberal Prime Minister of Britain, four times in office.

clue.text: Mythical Greek or Roman deadbeat

indicators.note: beat means battered, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with dead from the front of deadbeat

explanation.surface: Asking whether a figure is a mythical Greek or a lazy Roman good-for-nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deadbeat' splits: 'dead' joins 'Roman' as fodder and 'beat' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is the princess of Greek myth chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Flooded home, exactly when is not certain

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
something undated has no date, so its exact time is unknown

explanation.surface: A house swamped by water at some unknown moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated means overwhelmed with water, flooded.

clue.text: Examine prisoner initially arrested by bluebottle, say

indicators.note: being arrested by puts the prisoner's letter inside the insect

parts.note: a bluebottle is an example of an insect

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of prisoner

explanation.surface: A policeman, slangily a bluebottle, arrests a prisoner to look him over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottle' is old British slang for a policeman, but here it is the fly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look at closely, examine.

clue.text: Britain's downfall spoken of round Lvov

indicators.note: spoken of signals the phrase is said out loud

parts.note: UK is Britain, and rain is a downfall

explanation.surface: Talk of British decline in the context of the city of Lvov.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' suggests ruin but means rain falling; Lvov (Lviv) is a city in western Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The country surrounding the city of Lvov, which lies within its borders.

clue.text: Against Conservative leader as a buffoon

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Conservative

explanation.surface: An opponent of the Tory leader cast as a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Antic as a noun is an old word for a grotesque performer, a clown or buffoon.

clue.text: Flirted, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a variant, here a rearranged form of flirted

explanation.surface: A minimal remark that someone may have been flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FLIRTED are rearranged; flirting is also an instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To flirt is to dally or toy with someone, a kind of trifling with affections.

clue.text: Odour reported with scent?

parts.note: said aloud, odour sounds like the French eau de, which with this city's name gives a well-known scent

explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Cologne is a scent, named after the German city of Cologne.

clue.text: Bush mad? That's about right!

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes around the letter for right
mad means crazed, so the letters of bush are scrambled

explanation.surface: A jibe that a president called Bush is crazy, and that this is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' scrambles BUSH to SHUB, which goes 'about' R; the whole clue also defines the answer, a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, a bush.

clue.text: Flier's annoyed with demand for payment

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a bill is a demand for payment

explanation.surface: Someone irritated at receiving an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbill is a finch with crossed mandibles, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Hillside is almost bright

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short of its final letter

parts.note: clever means bright

explanation.surface: A hillside described as nearly sunny.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleve is a dialect word for a cliff or steep hillside.

clue.text: Worries about icy pillar

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: cares are worries

explanation.surface: Concerns about a column of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A serac is a pinnacle of ice on a glacier, a pillar of ice.

clue.text: Fastidious person finds English painting heartless

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter

parts.note: a painting is a picture

explanation.surface: A fussy critic dismisses an English painting as lacking feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle T of PICTURE, leaving PICURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is someone of refined, discriminating taste in food and drink.

clue.text: It enabled Wyatt to hear — or not!

definitions.text: It enabled Wyatt to hear — or not!

parts.note: Wyatt Earp, the Wild West lawman
a lug is slang for an ear, the organ used to hear

explanation.surface: A Wild West lawman's means of hearing, or of not hearing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as Earp's lug, it is what let Wyatt hear; the actual object stops you hearing, hence 'or not!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug is a plug put in the ear to block out sound.

clue.text: Device for foot-related operation

parts.note: sounds medical, like a tool for a foot operation, but means a lever worked by the foot to run a machine

explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a lever pressed by the foot to drive a machine such as a sewing machine.

clue.text: A small amount one takes to end it all in a depressed state

parts.note: cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small amount
I is the Roman numeral for one
to die is to end it all

explanation.surface: Someone taking a small dose to commit suicide while deeply depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidie is spiritual sloth or apathy, a listless depressed condition.
